instructions.available: A graphical desktop is available through the desktop_* tools.
instructions.accessibility: For standard apps, read desktop_accessibility_tree before taking a screenshot and click elements by ref; use screenshots for canvas, video and visual checks.
instructions.unavailable: The graphical desktop tools are unavailable. If the user asks for computer use, tell them: ${hint}

resources.name: desktop-screen
resources.title: Desktop screen
resources.description: Current screenshot of the machine's graphical desktop. Coordinates are pixels in the latest desktop_screenshot image (origin top-left).

tools.name: desktop_screenshot
tools.description: Capture the machine's graphical desktop. Returns an image plus its width and height. Coordinates are pixels in the latest desktop_screenshot image (origin top-left). If your client cannot see images in tool results, open the MCP resource desktop://screen instead and reopen it to refresh.

tools.name: desktop_zoom
tools.description: Capture a region of the desktop at higher detail, for reading small text. The region uses screenshot coordinates; the returned image is magnified and its pixels are not click coordinates.

tools.name: desktop_click
tools.description: Move the pointer and click. Coordinates are pixels in the latest desktop_screenshot image (origin top-left). Use count 2 for a double click. Modifiers are held during the click (ctrl, shift, alt, super).

screenshot.description: Return a screenshot after the action. Defaults to false.

settleMs.description: Wait before the follow-up screenshot. Defaults to 300.

tools.name: desktop_drag
tools.description: Press a mouse button at one point, move to another and release. Coordinates are pixels in the latest desktop_screenshot image (origin top-left).

screenshot.description: Return a screenshot after the action. Defaults to false.

settleMs.description: Wait before the follow-up screenshot. Defaults to 300.

tools.name: desktop_move
tools.description: Move the pointer without clicking, for example to reveal hover menus. Coordinates are pixels in the latest desktop_screenshot image (origin top-left).

screenshot.description: Return a screenshot after the action. Defaults to false.

settleMs.description: Wait before the follow-up screenshot. Defaults to 300.

tools.name: desktop_scroll
tools.description: Scroll with the mouse wheel at a point. Amount is wheel clicks (about 3 lines each). Coordinates are pixels in the latest desktop_screenshot image (origin top-left).

screenshot.description: Return a screenshot after the action. Defaults to false.

settleMs.description: Wait before the follow-up screenshot. Defaults to 300.

tools.name: desktop_type
tools.description: Type text into the focused window as keyboard input. Click the target field first. Use desktop_key for Enter, Tab and shortcuts.

screenshot.description: Return a screenshot after the action. Defaults to false.

settleMs.description: Wait before the follow-up screenshot. Defaults to 300.

tools.name: desktop_key
tools.description: Press keys or shortcuts in order, for example ["ctrl+l"], ["Enter"] or ["ctrl+shift+t"]. Names: letters, digits, Enter, Escape, Tab, Backspace, Delete, Space, Up, Down, Left, Right, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown, F1-F24, and modifiers ctrl, shift, alt, super joined with +.

screenshot.description: Return a screenshot after the action. Defaults to false.

settleMs.description: Wait before the follow-up screenshot. Defaults to 300.

tools.name: desktop_list_windows
tools.description: List visible top-level windows with id, title, bounds in screenshot coordinates and focus.

tools.name: desktop_focus_window
tools.description: Raise and focus a window by id from desktop_list_windows.

screenshot.description: Return a screenshot after the action. Defaults to false.

settleMs.description: Wait before the follow-up screenshot. Defaults to 300.

tools.name: desktop_launch
tools.description: Start a GUI application on the desktop, detached. Pass the executable and arguments separately; no shell is used. Example: {"command":"google-chrome","args":["https://example.com"]}. settleMs defaults to 2000 here, since applications take longer to appear.

screenshot.description: Return a screenshot after the action. Defaults to false.

settleMs.description: Wait before the follow-up screenshot. Defaults to 300.

accessibilityTools.name: desktop_screenshot
accessibilityTools.description: Capture the machine's graphical desktop. Returns an image plus its width and height. Coordinates are pixels in the latest desktop_screenshot image (origin top-left). If your client cannot see images in tool results, open the MCP resource desktop://screen instead and reopen it to refresh.

accessibilityTools.name: desktop_zoom
accessibilityTools.description: Capture a region of the desktop at higher detail, for reading small text. The region uses screenshot coordinates; the returned image is magnified and its pixels are not click coordinates.

accessibilityTools.name: desktop_click
accessibilityTools.description: Move the pointer and click. Coordinates are pixels in the latest desktop_screenshot image (origin top-left). Use count 2 for a double click. Modifiers are held during the click (ctrl, shift, alt, super). Pass either x and y, or the ref of an element from desktop_accessibility_tree to click its centre; a ref fails if the element is gone or off screen.

ref.description: Element ref from desktop_accessibility_tree, such as "r12".

screenshot.description: Return a screenshot after the action. Defaults to false.

settleMs.description: Wait before the follow-up screenshot. Defaults to 300.

accessibilityTools.name: desktop_accessibility_tree
accessibilityTools.description: Read the accessibility tree of the focused window as text, one element per line: ref, role, quoted name, value, bounds as @x,y widthxheight in screenshot coordinates, and states. Pass window (from desktop_list_windows) for another window, or ref to read one subtree. For standard apps it is usually cheaper than a screenshot and gives refs that desktop_click accepts. Refs stay valid while their element exists. Canvas, video, games and some apps expose little or nothing; use desktop_screenshot there and to check visual results. Defaults: interactiveOnly true, maxDepth 30, maxNodes 300.

ref.description: Element ref from desktop_accessibility_tree, such as "r12".

interactiveOnly.description: Only controls you can act on. Set false to include labels, headings and text.
